title: Lesson 3 Quiz: Carbon Taxes and Government Intervention
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not yet reviewed by a human (admin); do not give to students.

Comprehensive audit: q4 states demand sensitivity relative to supply (incidence depends on relative elasticity) and is retagged intermediate (one-step interpretation). Independent review follow-up: q4 now gives elasticity values so the comparison must be inferred. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

questions.prompt: Compared with command-and-control regulation that sets the same emission standard for every factory, what is the main advantage of a pollution tax?

choices.text: Firms that can cut cheaply cut more, so the same reduction costs less overall
The government can set the total amount of reduction precisely in advance
Paying the tax makes the pollution damage disappear on the spot
Each firm is assigned the same amount of pollution to cut

questions.prompt: In an emissions trading system (cap-and-trade), what does the government set directly?

choices.text: The price of a single emissions permit
The abatement technology each firm has to use
The amount each individual firm has to cut

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Demand is Qd = 150 − 3P and supply is Qs = 10 + 2P, and with no tax the equilibrium price is $28. If producers are charged a carbon tax of $10 per unit, what price do consumers pay, in dollars? (Enter a number only.)

Hypothetical example: A carbon tax charged to producers is placed on gasoline. At the market equilibrium, the price elasticity of demand is −0.2 and the price elasticity of supply is 1.5. Which statement best describes the tax burden?

choices.text: Producers bear most of the burden
Producers, who legally pay the tax, bear the entire burden
Consumers bear most of the burden
Consumers and producers split the burden exactly in half

questions.prompt: In the same market as q3, assume each unit produced causes $10 of external damage. With a carbon tax of $10, what is the change in social welfare (avoided external damage − loss within the market), in dollars? (Enter a number only.)
